inputs: All 576 NESSIE Set 1 vectors (128 for 128-bit keys, 192 for 192-bit keys, 256 for 256-bit keys), their Iterated 100 results, and the Iterated 1000 result of the first vector of each key length
expected: Every encryption matches the printed ciphertext, every decryption returns the printed plaintext, all 576 Iterated 100 results match, and the three Iterated 1000 results match
limitations: Set 1 varies one key bit per vector but uses a fixed zero plaintext; it tests key avalanche and conformance, not cryptanalytic security.

inputs: The first 32 Set 2 vectors, the first 32 Set 3 vectors and both Set 4 vectors for each of the 128/192/256-bit key lengths (198 vectors)
expected: Every encryption matches the printed ciphertext and every decryption returns the printed plaintext; the Set 2 vectors use a zero key with variable plaintext, Set 3 uses key equal to repeated plaintext byte, and Set 4 uses fixed incrementing key/plaintext
limitations: Only the first 32 of the printed Set 2 and Set 3 vectors are used; the remaining vectors are not transcribed.

inputs: The 128/192/256-bit key-padding samples, the eight padded words, the 132-prekey recurrence with phi=0x9e3779b9 and rotl 11, and the 33 S-box-derived subkeys
expected: padKey places the 1 bit at position 128/192 (256 unchanged), keySchedule returns 132 prekeys and 33 four-word subkeys, independently recomputing the recurrence and K_i reproduces the schedule, and the 128-bit key 80000000000000000000000000000000 gives K0=6F539CD2 A7A3A3CE D29591ED 8EDF7292
limitations: The paper does not print subkey values; K0 is computed from the specified padding, recurrence and S-box, and the schedule is verified indirectly through all NESSIE ciphertexts.

inputs: The eight 4-bit S-box tables, their differential/linear distributions and nonlinear order, the LT and inverse LT, three keys and eight deterministic plaintexts, and byte-order/padding samples
expected: All S-boxes are permutations with maximum differential probability at most 1/4, no one-bit to one-bit differential, linear bias at most 1/4 (one-bit at most 1/8) and maximum nonlinear order 3; LT and inverse LT invert; all 24 round trips succeed; the 128-bit key pads with a 1 at position 128; a non-zero big-endian negative control gives a different ciphertext
limitations: The S-box and LT checks are structural; round trips are deterministic and do not test modes, protocols, key management, side channels or randomness.
